title: Evidence-guided receptor-state selection
one_sentence_claim: Adaptive evidence integration can select GPCR receptor conformations that improve screening enrichment over strong fixed baselines.
problem: Receptor conformation selection can materially alter GPCR virtual-screening performance.

gap.statement: Target-specific structure selection may require evidence integration beyond a single predefined structure-selection rule.

hypothesis: An adaptive evidence-guided selector will improve held-out-target enrichment relative to fixed single-structure and naive ensemble baselines.
mechanistic_rationale: Different receptor states expose distinct pocket geometries and interaction patterns, so target-specific evidence may identify structures better matched to active ligands.
method: Retrieve candidate receptor structures, integrate structural and pharmacological evidence, perform bounded retrospective docking, and select a receptor or small ensemble before held-out screening.

evaluation.success_criterion: Consistent improvement over strong fixed baselines across held-out targets.
evaluation.failure_criterion: No reproducible improvement or no transfer to held-out targets.
evaluation.validation_notes: Use target-level separation and repeated runs where stochastic decisions are involved.

falsification_condition: The hypothesis is unsupported if adaptive selection does not outperform strong fixed or expert baselines on held-out targets.
critical_assumptions: Candidate receptor structures span functionally relevant states.
Retrospective ligand data are sufficiently informative for target-level evaluation.
main_risks: Data leakage between selection and evaluation.
Apparent gains may arise from docking-engine bias rather than improved state selection.
verification_queue: Search for prior adaptive GPCR receptor-state selection systems.
Verify availability of held-out target benchmarks with suitable actives and decoys.
orthogonality_rationale: This candidate studies receptor-state selection rather than pipeline composition, computational-budget allocation, or scientific discovery of target regimes.

agent_fields.non_static_decision: Choose which receptor structures to retain and whether additional evidence or docking tests are needed.
agent_fields.state_dependent_adaptation: Intermediate enrichment and pocket checks can alter the next evidence-gathering or selection action.
agent_fields.scientific_autonomy: The system makes target-specific receptor-selection decisions rather than only executing a predetermined structure list.
